summary: GiftCookie is a subclass of Cookie that adds gift-wrapping behaviour: one public method walks through the whole packaging routine by calling three small private helper methods, each responsible for a single step.

lines.text: The `extends` keyword makes GiftCookie a specialised kind of Cookie, so it automatically inherits Cookie's fields and methods such as `getFlavor()`.
A subclass does not inherit constructors, so GiftCookie declares its own that accepts the flavor a caller supplies.
This hands the flavor up to the Cookie constructor so the inherited part of the object is properly initialised; it must be the first statement in the constructor.
This is the one method outside code needs to call, and it acts as the recipe that orders the individual packaging steps.
Calling a method of the same object needs no dot prefix, which keeps the recipe easy to read top to bottom.
The note travels from the caller through `packageCookie` into the helper, showing how a parameter can be passed along a chain of method calls.
Returning a confirmation string lets the caller report or test the outcome instead of relying only on printed output.
Marking the helper `private` means only GiftCookie can call it, which hides the internal steps and leaves `packageCookie` as the single public entry point.

lines.code: System.out.println("Packaged " + getFlavor() + " cookie in a box.");
lines.text: `getFlavor()` is inherited from Cookie, so the subclass can read the flavor without knowing how the parent stores it.
The `\"` escape sequence puts literal double quotes into the output, since a bare quote would end the string early.
